## Overview

Complete CLI over the entire Keboola API. Two command layers:

- **Layer 1 — Atomic commands** (136 commands): 1:1 mapping to every Keboola API method across 16 services
- **Layer 2 — Logical units** (11 units, 33 commands): High-level domain-oriented commands with table formatting and smart defaults

## Authentication

```bash
kbc auth login --token <STORAGE_API_TOKEN> --url <STACK_URL>
```

Or via environment variables: `KBC_STORAGE_TOKEN`, `KBC_STORAGE_URL`

## Logical Units

### `kbc component` — Manage components, configurations, and configuration rows

Use when working with Keboola components (extractors, writers, transformations, applications). Typical workflow: list components → pick one → list configs → show/create config → manage rows. Components are the building blocks of Keboola pipelines — each has configurations that define how it runs.

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `kbc component list` | List all components in the project |
| `kbc component show <componentId>` | Show component details (schema, documentation) |
| `kbc component configs <componentId>` | List configurations for a component |
| `kbc component config-show <componentId> <configId>` | Show configuration details |
| `kbc component config-create <componentId>` | Create a new configuration |
| `kbc component config-delete <componentId> <configId>` | Delete a configuration |
| `kbc component config-search` | Search configurations across all components |
| `kbc component row-create <componentId> <configId>` | Create a configuration row |
| `kbc component row-delete <componentId> <configId> <rowId>` | Delete a configuration row |

### `kbc job` — Manage jobs (run, list, monitor)

Use when checking pipeline execution status. Typical workflow: list recent jobs (optionally filter by status/component) → show job details for debugging. Jobs represent individual runs of components or flows.

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `kbc job list` | List recent jobs |
| `kbc job show <jobId>` | Show job details (status, results, metrics) |

### `kbc bucket` — Manage storage buckets

Use when managing storage organization. Typical workflow: list buckets → create bucket (in/out stage) → manage tables inside. Buckets are top-level containers in Keboola Storage that group related tables.

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `kbc bucket list` | List all buckets in the project |
| `kbc bucket show <bucketId>` | Show bucket details |
| `kbc bucket create` | Create a new bucket |
| `kbc bucket delete <bucketId>` | Delete a bucket |

### `kbc table` — Manage storage tables

Use when working with data stored in Keboola Storage. Typical workflow: list tables (optionally filter by bucket) → show table details (columns, metadata) → preview data. Tables hold the actual data rows inside buckets.

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `kbc table list` | List tables in a bucket |
| `kbc table show <tableId>` | Show table details (columns, metadata) |
| `kbc table preview <tableId>` | Preview table data |

### `kbc flow` — Manage flows (orchestrations)

Use when managing orchestrations/pipelines. Typical workflow: list flows → show flow details. Flows (formerly orchestrations) define multi-step pipelines that run components in sequence or parallel.

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `kbc flow list` | List all flows in the project |
| `kbc flow show <flowId>` | Show flow details (phases, tasks, schedule) |

### `kbc transformation` — Manage transformations (SQL, Python, R)

Use when working with data transformations (SQL, Python, R). Typical workflow: list transformations → show details. Transformations are a special component type that process data using code.

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `kbc transformation list` | List all transformations in the project |

### `kbc secret` — Manage project secrets (vault)

Use when managing project-level secrets stored in Keboola Vault. Typical workflow: list secrets → create/delete secrets. Secrets are encrypted key-value pairs available to components at runtime.

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `kbc secret list` | List all secrets in the project |
| `kbc secret create` | Create a new secret |
| `kbc secret delete <secretId>` | Delete a secret |

### `kbc branch` — Manage development branches

Use when working with development branches. Typical workflow: list branches → create branch → work in isolation → merge. Branches allow isolated development without affecting production data.

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `kbc branch list` | List all branches |
| `kbc branch create` | Create a new development branch |
| `kbc branch delete <branchId>` | Delete a development branch |

### `kbc token` — Manage Storage API tokens

Use when managing Storage API tokens and permissions. Typical workflow: list tokens to see who has access. Tokens control authentication and authorization for API access.

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `kbc token verify` | Verify current token and show project info |

### `kbc workspace` — Manage workspaces (sandboxes)

Use when managing interactive workspaces (sandboxes). Typical workflow: list workspaces → create workspace → use for development. Workspaces provide interactive environments (Jupyter, RStudio, etc.) connected to project data.

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `kbc workspace list` | List all workspaces |
| `kbc workspace show` | Show workspace details |
| `kbc workspace delete` | Delete a workspace |

### `kbc file` — Manage file uploads

Use when managing file uploads in Keboola Storage. Typical workflow: list files → show file details. Files are used for importing/exporting data and storing artifacts.

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `kbc file list` | List recent file uploads |
| `kbc file delete <fileId>` | Delete a file |

## Hand-Written Units

These units have custom logic beyond simple API calls:

### `kbc data-app` — Manage Data Apps (deploy, logs, start/stop, open in browser)

Use for deploying and managing Data Apps. Typical workflow: list apps → use <app-id> → deploy --follow → logs → open. Supports full lifecycle management including deploy with log streaming.

### `kbc auth` — Authentication (login, logout, status, profiles)

Use to authenticate with Keboola. Run `kbc auth login` to set up credentials. Supports multiple profiles for different stacks.

### `kbc use` — Set active Data App context

Use to set the active Data App ID so subsequent commands don't need --app flag.

### `kbc secrets` — Manage Data App secrets (list, set, delete, import from .env)

Use to manage environment variables/secrets for Data Apps. Supports bulk import from .env files.

### `kbc runs` — View Data App deployment runs

Use to inspect deployment history and run details for Data Apps.

### `kbc config` — CLI configuration (show, set, git integration)

Use to manage CLI settings and git integration for Data App deployment.

### `kbc api` — Raw API calls (any method, any URL)

Use for advanced/custom API calls not covered by other units. Supports any HTTP method and arbitrary URL paths.
